| ὁ τλήμων Ὀδυσεύς (10.231) | "enduring Odysseus" | "enduring Odysseus" | "much-enduring" (reserved for πολύτλας), "long-suffering" (turned down in the Odyssey table), "wretched", "hardy"; τλήμων keeps the table’s τλήμονα θυμὸν ἔχων "enduring" (5.670) |
| ἄφαλον τε καὶ ἄλλοφον (κυνέην, 10.258; φάλος "ridge of the helmet", sense not certain) | "ridgeless and crestless" | "without ridge and without crest" (+ note: φάλος uncertain) | "bossless", "plumeless", "without plate" (each decides the unknown); follows ἀμφίφαλον "two-ridged" (5.743), λόφος "crest" |
| καταῖτυξ (10.258; origin not known) | "kataityx" | "kataityx" (+ note: the word is of unknown origin) | "skull-cap", "leather cap", "cap-helm" (each fixes a meaning the Greek does not give) |
| θαλερῶν αἰζηῶν (10.259) | "flourishing vigorous young men" | "flourishing young men" | "lusty", "blooming" (reserved for θαλερὸς γάμος), "strong" (αἰζηός is "vigorous young man", 5.92, 8.298) |
| ἐρῳδιός (δεξιὸν ἐρῳδιόν, 10.274) | "heron" | "a heron on their right" | "egret", "bittern"; δεξιός "on the right" (the lucky side), kept visible in both layers |
| νύκτα δι’ ὀρφναίην (10.276) | "through the murky night" | "through the murky night" | "dark", "black" (kept for μέλας / μέλαινα), "gloomy"; ὀρφναῖος "murky" |
| ὑπόρρηνον (ὄϊν … θῆλυν ὑπόρρηνον, 10.216; ὑπό + ῥήν "lamb") | "with a lamb beneath her" | "with a lamb at her side" (+ note: the usual explanation) | "suckling", "woolly", "fleece-bearing"; the usual explanation of the word |
| κτέρας (τῇ μὲν κτέρας οὐδὲν ὁμοῖον, 10.216; singular of the usual κτέρεα) | "possession" | "possession" | "treasure", "honour", "gift" (δόσις); the singular is rare |
| ὑπουράνιον κλέος (10.212) | "under-heaven fame" | "great fame under the whole sky" | "world-wide renown", "fame to the heavens"; ὑπό + οὐρανός, with κλέος "fame" (as 2.486, 4.197) |
| βράσσων τε νόος, λεπτὴ δέ τε μῆτις (10.226; βράσσων usually taken as comparative of βραχύς) | "rather short" · "thin" | "rather short" · "thin" | "scanty", "weak", "slight" (each loses the picture), "subtle" and "fine" (λεπτή is not praise here); μῆτις keeps "cunning" |
| ἄνεται (νὺξ ἄνεται, 10.251; usually taken as from ἀνύω, sense not certain) | "is being spent" | "is far spent" (+ note: sense not certain) | "is waning", "is going by", "is ending"; the usual explanation |
| παροίχωκεν δὲ πλέων νὺξ τῶν δύο μοιράων (10.252–253; construction of πλέων with the genitive disputed) | "gone by is the night, more than the two parts" | "the night has run on past its two parts" (+ note: construction disputed) | "two parts of the night have passed" (supplies the arithmetic the Greek leaves to the next line), "most of the night" |
| ὣς εἰπόνθ’ ὅπλοισιν ἔνι δεινοῖσιν ἐδύτην (10.254, 10.272 with the first words changed) | "So having spoken, in dread arms the two clad themselves." · "And the two, when then in dread arms they had clad themselves," | "So they spoke, and the two clad themselves in their dread arms." · "And when the two had clad themselves in their dread arms," | "put on", "armed themselves" (lose the dual and the δύω "go into"), "fearful", "terrible" (reserved for αἰνός); δεινός keeps "dread" (7.245) |
| φάσγανον ἄμφηκες (10.256) | "a two-edged sword" | "a two-edged sword" | "double-edged", "sharp on both sides"; φάσγανον is "sword" |
| ἔκτοσθε … λευκοὶ ὀδόντες ἀργιόδοντος ὑὸς θαμέες ἔχον ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα (10.263–264) | "on the outside white teeth of a white-toothed boar held thick-set here and there" | "on the outside the white teeth of a white-toothed boar were set close together, here and there" | "gleaming tusks", "bright-toothed" (turned down for ἀργιόδων, the table’s "white-toothed", 8.60, 8.476); θαμέες "thick-set"; "boar" against the Odyssey table’s "pig" for ἀργιόδων ὗς (8.476) and ἀργιόδοντας ὕας (8.60): kept as "boar" because the tusks on a helmet are a wild boar’s, flagged for the owner to decide whether the table needs a line |
| πῖλος ἀρήρει (10.265) | "felt was fitted" | "was fitted a lining of felt" | "padding", "wool"; πῖλος is "felt"; "lining" is supplied by the picture of the helmet’s inside |
| ἐξέλετ’ … πυκινὸν δόμον ἀντιτορήσας (10.267; ἀντιτορέω "bore through") | "took out, a solid house having broken through" | "breaking into his solid house" | "close-built", "strong" (the first draft), "pierced", "storming"; follows the table’s πυκινὸς δόμος "solid house" (7.81); the Iliad table sets πυκινός "solid" against "shrewd" of a plan |
| βιὸν ἠδὲ φαρέτρην καὶ ξίφος (10.260–261) | "a bow and a quiver and a sword" | "a bow and a quiver and a sword" | "arrows" (kept for ὀϊστοί), "sheath"; βιός "bow" (the accent tells it from βίος "life") |
| ἅσσα μητιόωσι · ἦε πόλιν δὲ ἂψ ἀναχωρήσουσιν (10.208–210; indirect question) | "what things they are planning" · "or to the city back they will withdraw" | "what they are planning" · "or will withdraw again to the city" | "intend", "counsel" (reserved for βουλεύω); μητιάω is built on μῆτις "cunning" |
| σπεῖό μοι (10.285; aorist imperative of ἕπομαι) | "go with me" | "go with me" | "attend me", "follow me", "be at my side" (each adds a rank); ἕσπεο "you went with" |
